SUBJECT:  APPROVE RENEWAL OF GENERAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  BETWEEN THE CITY OF PALMDALE AND THE COUNTY OF LOS
  ANGELES

ISSUE
Approve the renewal of General Services Agreement No. A-8247 between the City of
Palmdale and the County of Los Angeles.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the renewal of General Services No. Agreement A-8247 between the City
  of Palmdale and the County of Los Angeles.

BACKGROUND
The General Services Agreement (GSA) is generic in nature and provides the authority
for the County to provide services requested by the City. It also specifies the method by
which the City requests and pays for services.

DISCUSSION
The current GSA with the County of Los Angeles expires June 30, 2023. The renewal is
for a 5-year agreement and will be valid from July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2028.
Services provided by the GSA are requested by the City on an “as needed” basis.
Sample services are predatory animal control and a variety of public works activities
such as Weed Abatement, Bridge Inspection and/or Maintenance and Infrastructure
Design and Construction. Specific service such as law enforcement, public health, code
enforcement and animal control are handled by separate agreements.
No service or function performed under the agreement will be provided unless the City
specifically requests the work to be done.
 Report to Mayor and City Council

  AMOUNT OF THE AGREEMENT BY $95,000 NOT TO EXCEED THE
  SUM OF $335,000 AND EXTEND CONTRACT TERM.

ISSUE
Approve First Amendment to provide temporary electrical and general services for
special events with Henisey Electric (A-6998) to increase the total amount of the
agreement by $95,000, not to exceed the sum of $335,000, and extend contract term.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve First Amendment to provide temporary electrical and general services
  for special events with Henisey Electric (A-6998) to increase the total amount of
  the agreement by $95,000, not to exceed the sum of $335,000, and extend
  contract term.

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or her designee, to approve First Amendment to
  Agreement No. A-6998 with Henisey Electric.

BACKGROUND
Henisey Electric provides temporary generated power distribution and equipment
required to supplement existing power to meet contractual obligations of performers,
vendors, and renters for large scale events. Examples of services include developing an
electrical distribution plan tailored to event needs, managing power supply for the duration
of the event, providing power to tour buses, managing house power, and avoiding
overload, troubleshoot power malfunctions and emergencies. Henisey Electric provides
all electrical equipment needed, such as commercial grade power generators,
commercial grade cables and connections, distribution power boxes, temporary light
trees, projection equipment, audio equipment and portable outdoor cooling units. The
original agreement was fully executed on July 1, 2020, for a three-year term, with a two-
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Amendment No. 1 for Agreement No. A-6998
May 17, 2023
Page 2

year amendment option. The agreement is set to expire on June 30, 2023, and we are
seeking to exercise the first amendment option to extend for one additional year.

DISCUSSION
Henisey Electric provides a licensed, bonded, and insured electrician which meets all
State and Federal regulations. The Contract requires equipment provided to be inspected
and certified for use in the State of California. Contracting with Henisey Electric alleviates
the City from the cost of purchasing, replacing, maintaining, transporting, and fueling
electrical equipment.
Henisey Electric has an excellent service history and has assisted in the production of
City events for many years, as well as assisting the Maintenance Division with various
installation projects. Henisey Electric is a local small business and has been very
responsive to the City’s needs.

FISCAL IMPACT
Approval of these recommendations would allow Henisey Electric to provide the required
temporary electrical services and equipment for outdoor events and City facilities. The
term of the First Amendment is for one (1) additional year, with an increase of an
additional Ninety-Five Thousand Dollars ($95,000), not to exceed the sum of Three-
Hundred Thirty-Five Thousand Dollars ($335,000) over a four (4) year period.
Expenditure funds are subject to the approved fiscal year budget. Expenses for electrical
services could be charged to the following accounts, dependent upon event type:

The contract fee schedule is updated to reflect market changes consistent with local and
industry trends. Fuel and equipment rental charges have not increased since the
beginning of the contract term. Labor has increased 11%, following associated Division
of Industrial Relations requirements. Equipment rental charges are inclusive of delivery
and fuel has increased an average of 14%.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE SUPPLEMENTAL AGREEMENT NO. 1 WITH SULLY
  MILLER CONTRACTING CO., FOR PN 698, AVENUE R COMPLETE
  STREETS PROJECT, IN THE AMOUNT OF $889,797.42.

ISSUE
Approve Supplemental Agreement No. 1 with Sully Miller Contracting Co., for PN 698,
Avenue R Complete Streets Project, in the amount of $889,797.42.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
A. Approve Supplemental Agreement No. 1 to Agreement No. A-7596 with Sully Miller
  Contracting Co., for PN 698, Avenue R Complete Streets Project, in the amount of
  $889,797.42.

B. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Supplemental Agreement No.
  1 to Agreement No. A-7596 with Sully Miller Contracting Co., including non-
  substantive changes.

C. Authorize the transfer of $172,487, of unappropriated Gas Tax Fund Balance into
  Account S0058201.

D. Authorize a budget increase to Metro Measure M Earmark grant funds in the amount
  of $35,741 to Account S0058209.

BACKGROUND
Capital Improvement Project No. 698, Avenue R Complete Streets Project, includes
roadway widening improvements along Avenue R from Sierra Highway to 25th Street
East. These improvements include sidewalk gap closures, driveway and curb ramp
construction, traffic signal modification, streetlight improvements, storm drain
improvements, roadway rehabilitation, and signing & striping.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Supplemental Agreement No. 1, Agreement No. A-7596
May 17, 2023
Page 2

This Capital Improvement Project was awarded to Sully Miller Contracting Co. at the
March 2, 2022, City Council Meeting in the amount of $10,690,000. Staff anticipated that
construction would take approximately 400 working days from the date the City issued
the Notice to Proceed and estimated that work would be scheduled between June 2022
and November 2023. Award was made to Sully Miller with the assumption that all
Southern California Edison utility relocation would be completed by Spring 2022. In the
time since the bid award, SCE has reassigned three (3) project planners to the job and
cited a delay due to an environmental concern. Despite repeated requests and follow-up
by City Staff, Southern California Edison did not schedule their work until November 9,
2022 and did not complete their work until February 7, 2023. Additional utilities removals
on the existing SCE lines (i.e. Charter Communications, AT&T and Crown Castle) have
also delayed the start of this project. It is anticipated that construction will begin in June
2023.

DISCUSSION
Supplemental Agreement No. 1 approves one (1) change order as outlined below.
Change Order 003 includes a cost escalation to account for the lengthy delay in the start
of construction caused by Southern California Edison’s delay in relocating their
transmission and distribution poles and increases the contract price. Cost increases are
for the changes in material cost, prevailing wage rates, and trucking costs, by
$889,797.42, as more specifically detailed below:

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

A. Award construction agreement with Landscape Structures Inc. for PN 881, Palmdale
  Oasis Park Playground Project, in the amount of $646,624.78.

B. Authorize the City Manager, or their designee, to execute Agreement No. A-8317 with
  Landscape Structures Inc. including non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
Project No. 881, Palmdale Oasis Park Playground Project, includes a new playground
to be constructed and installed at the Palmdale Oasis Park, located at 3850 E. Ave S.
The new ADA accessible playground will be approximately 10,000 square feet with
Engineered Wood Fiber (EWF) mulch flooring that adheres to the basic requirements of
the American with Disabilities Act (ADA) and will feature one section with equipment
geared toward children 2-5 years of age and a second section with equipment geared
toward children 5-12 years of age. A unique playground element includes a wheelchair
accessible “We-Go-Swing”. This accessible swing moves in a traditional back and forth
direction as opposed to side to side. The playground will be located adjacent to the
existing Palmdale Oasis Recreation Center and will enhance the open field area.
Additional park enhancements include a picnic table, trash cans, and an ADA accessible
concrete sidewalk. It is anticipated that construction will take approximately 4 months
from the date the City issues the Notice to Proceed and is projected to be completed by
Fall 2023.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Award construction agreement with PlayCore Wisconsin, Inc. dba: GameTime, for
  PN 883, Desert Sands Park Playground Project, in the amount of $776,875.88.

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or their designee, to execute Agreement No. A-8259

BACKGROUND
Project No. 883, Desert Sands Park Playground Project, includes the replacement of play
equipment in an existing playground at the Desert Sands Park, located at 39117 3rd
Street East. It is anticipated that construction will take approximately 4 months days from
the date the City issues the Notice to Proceed and is projected to be complete in late
summer 2023.

DISCUSSION
There is currently $2,470,000 in Measure AV Funds, in Account No. P0109157, that will
be utilized to construct an ADA accessible playground located at Desert Sands Park. The
new playground equipment has one section geared toward ages 2-5 years of age and a
second section geared toward 5-12 years of age. A unique enhancement includes an
obstacle course along with sensory wave seat sliders, sky run zip track, agility pods,
climbing elements, spinners, and slides. This equipment will be replacing old and
outdated equipment that has been in place since the early 2000’s. The existing

BACKGROUND
In accordance with the Revenue and Tax Code (Sections 99 and 99.01) any time there
is a jurisdictional change which results in a special district providing new service not
previously provided to an area, the law requires the governing bodies of all local
agencies that receive a portion of that property tax determine by resolution the amount
of the annual tax increase to be transferred to that special district. The existing tax
revenue based on the properties assessed value received by agencies will not
change. This resolution only affects a percentage of the future revenue agencies
would receive based on the increased property valuation assessment.

DISCUSSION

In the attached letter dated September 14, 2022, the County Sanitation District has
requested that the City of Palmdale enter into a tax sharing agreement for the
annexation of parcel numbers 3128-015-902 and 3128-015-900 as shown in Exhibit A.
The proposed development is located at the southeast corner of 10th Street West and
Avenue M has requested annexation into the County Sanitation District (CSD) No. 14.
This annexation request is a condition of the developments entitlement and required
prior to receiving sewer service.

The execution of the attached Joint Resolution will approve the tax sharing agreement
by the City for the annexation of the subject property into the County Sanitation District
No. 14 boundary. All public agencies and special districts that currently receive
property tax revenues for these parcels execute and are a party to the same Joint
Resolution.

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-032 authorizing
the Mayor to execute the Joint Tax Sharing Resolution entitled Annexation No. 14-438
with the County Sanitation District No. 14 for the parcels.

FISCAL IMPACT
The current property tax share ratio for the City of Palmdale within the area of these
parcels is 0.066247854 (6.6248%). This Council action will allocate 0.004576613
percent (0.4577%) of any future tax increase on these parcels to the County Sanitation
District No. 14. This results in a net City tax share rate of 0.065685608 (6.5685%) for
the same tax increase amount. For example, a tax increase based on the assessed

  CITY OF PALMDALE
  MEASURE AV OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE
  BYLAWS

ARTICLE I – ESTABLISHMENT AND PURPOSE

  A. Name. Official name of the committee shall be Measure AV Oversight Committee

  (the “Committee”)

  B. Compensation. Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.08.030(H),

  members of the Committee shall be entitled to compensation in the sum of One

  Hundred Dollars ($100) for each meeting attended, provided, however, that no

  member shall be paid such compensation for attendance at more than two such

  meetings during any one calendar month. The chair of the committee shall be

  entitled to additional compensation of Fifty Dollars ($50) per meeting attended,

  limited to two meetings per calendar month. Compensation shall only be due and

  payable to Committee members (not alternates) who attend and participate in the

  committee meeting for which they request compensation. In addition, all

  members of the committee shall be entitled to compensation in the sum of One

  Hundred Dollars ($100) for attendance at each legally required training course.

  Reimbursement shall only be given for expenses actually incurred in connection

  with serving on the Committee.
   C. Establishment. Measure AV, approved in November 2020, calls for the

  establishment of a committee to ensure that all funds from the measure are

  appropriately used.

  D. Purpose. The purpose of this Committee is set forth in Measure AV. (Protecting

  Palmdale's long-term financial stability; maintaining essential city services;

  repairing streets/potholes; addressing homelessness; maintaining 911

  emergency response; keeping public areas safe/clean for all; retaining local

  businesses; protecting local water sources; maintaining veterans, senior, mental

  health, community programs; by establishing a ¾-cent sales tax; requiring citizen

  oversight, public spending disclosures; all funds used locally in Palmdale). These

  Bylaws are specifically made subject to the applicable provisions of Measure AV

  as to the duties and rights of the Committee. The Committee is subject to the

  Ralph M. Brown Public Meetings Act of the State of California and shall conduct

  its meetings in accordance with the provisions thereof.

  E. Administrative Support. The City shall give all necessary administrative support

  to the Committee, as is consistent with the Committee’s purpose.

  F. Duties. The duties of this Committee are:

  a. To ensure that all funds from the three-quarters cent sales tax are spent in

  accordance with Measure AV.

  b. To prepare an annual written report setting forth the purposes for which

  Measure AV funds were expended in the preceding year and the amount

  spent in each category.

ARTICLE II – POSITIONS AND TERMS
 A. Committee Members. Committee Members shall consist of seven (7) members

  and (2) alternates.

B. Committee Additions and Subtractions. The City Council may, by unanimous

  decision, vote to add or subtract the number of alternate members on the

  Committee.

C. Term Length. Each member of the Committee shall be appointed for a two (2)

  year term.

D. Term Limit. Committee members are limited to a three (3) term limit for serving

  on the Committee.

E. Committee Vacancy. Should a vacancy arise from a member resigning or other

  matters the following shall happen:

  a. The vacancy will be filled by a Committee alternate member.

  b. The Committee alternate member shall be picked by the City Council and

  voted in by majority vote.

  c. If a vacancy is filled, and there is greater than a year left on the term, it

  shall count as a full term for the appointed Committee Member’s term limit.

  If less than a year remains on the term, it shall not count towards the

  Committee Member’s term limit.

F. Forfeiture. Should any Committee member miss three (3) consecutive

  Committee meetings without any prior consent or notice to the Committee, they

  shall forfeit their membership on the Committee. All forfeited Committee positions

  shall be subject to Article II, Section E, for the purpose of their vacancy.
 G. Chair. The Committee shall appoint one member to serve as the Chair of the

  Committee by a simple majority vote. The Chair shall preside over all meetings of

  the Committee. The Chair is responsible for keeping order and decorum during

  the Committee’s meetings.

H. Vice-Chair. The Committee shall appoint one member to serve as the Vice-Chair

  of the Committee by simple majority vote. The Vice-Chair shall perform the duties

  of the chair in the absence or incapacity of the Chair, until such time as a new

  Chair is selected or appointed. Should both the Chair and Vice-Chair be absence

  or incapacitated, the Committee shall vote by simple majority to appoint an

  interim Chair and Vice-Chair for the purpose of that current meeting and any

  subsequent meetings until either the Chair or Vice-Chair are able to return to

  their duties.

I. Staff Secretary. City staff shall appoint one member to serve as the Staff

  Secretary of the Committee. The Staff Secretary shall keep the minutes of all

  official meetings of the Committee, which shall be open for inspection by any

  member of the public. The Staff Secretary shall sign reports and correspondence

  for the Committee, along with setting meeting dates; providing agendas to each

  Committee member prior to each official meeting. The Staff Secretary shall

  inform Committee members of all available data gathered by City staff pertinent

  to each item on said agenda. The Staff Secretary shall inform Committee

  members of the time and place of any special meeting. The Staff Secretary shall

  make available to the Committee all correspondence addressed to the

  Committee.
 ARTICLE III – MEETINGS

  A. Rules. All meetings will fall under rules set by the Ralph M. Brown Act (Cal. Gov’t

  Code §54950 et seq.) (“Brown Act”).

  B. Meeting Dates. The Measure AV Oversight Committee shall meet bi-monthly

  (i.e., every two (2) months), and as needed, to carry out its purpose. These set

  dates can be changed by resolution as needed.

  C. Specials Meetings and Emergency. Special Meetings can be called by the

  Chair or Vice Chair with five days prior notice. Emergency meetings can be

  called as needed.

  D. Open and Public Meetings. All meetings concerning all Committee actions and

  deliberations shall be open and allow for anyone in the public to attend.

  E. Agenda. An agenda shall be published to the public and sent out to each

  Committee member no less than seventy-two (72) hours before the meeting

  takes place. All agendas should include time, date, and location where the

  meeting(s) are to take place along with the type of meeting (Regular, Special, or

  Emergency). Any items not on the agenda will be placed in the non-agenda items

  portion of the meeting.

  F. Minutes. Minutes of the proceedings of the Committee and all documents

  received and reports issued shall be a matter of public record and be made

  available on an Internet website maintained by the Committee.
 ARTICLE IV. – CONDUCT OF MEETINGS
  A. Order of Business. The regular order of business shall be:

  1. Call to Order

  2. Public Comment

  3. Approval of Minutes from the previous meeting.

  4. Consideration and Action of Agenda Items

  5. Non-Agenda Items

  6. Adjournment

  The order of business can be modified as needed.

  B. Parliamentary Procedure. All proceedings before the Committee may be guided

  by the rules of parliamentary procedure set forth in Rosenberg’s Rules of Order,

  but failure to follow Rosenberg’s Rules of Order shall not affect the validity of any

  action or motion duly taken or adopted by the Committee at any lawfully held

  meeting.

  C. Presentations to the Committee. Any person desiring to address the

  Committee shall be requested, when recognized by the Chair, to give his or her

  name and address for the record. The Chair may, in the interest of facilitating the

  business of the Committee, set in advance of the presentation of testimony

  reasonable time limits for oral presentations. Persons may be required to submit

  written testimony in lieu of oral testimony if the Chair determines that a

  reasonable opportunity for oral presentations has been provided, and in such a

  case, the matter may be continued to a later date to allow a reasonable time for

  such submittals to occur.
   D. Attendance. Members shall be considered present at the Committee meeting if

  they are there physically, on the phone, or using a video conferencing

  application.

ARTICLE V. – VOTING AND QUORUM

  A. Roll Call Vote. A roll call vote may be required in voting upon any motion of the

  Committee at the discretion of the Chair.

  B. Quorum. A majority of the currently appointed members of the Committee shall

  constitute a quorum for the purpose of conducting its business and exercising its

  powers and for all other official purposes, except that less than a quorum may

  adjourn from time to time until a quorum is obtained.

  C. Number of Votes Required for Action. All actions require a motion and a

  second. No action or recommendation of the Committee shall be valid and binding

  unless a quorum is present, and the motion is approved by a simple majority of the

  members present. Each member shall have one vote. No votes may be cast by

  proxy. Tie votes shall be considered as denial of the motion.

  D. Conflicts of Interest. The Committee shall be subject to conflict of interest in

  accordance with the Fair Political Practices Act. City Councilpersons shall not vote

  for any person who presents a conflict of interest with them.

  E. Motion to Reconsider. The Committee may reconsider a matter during the

  meeting at which the vote was taken, provided all members who were present when

  the matter was discussed and voted upon are still present, all persons who

  addressed the Committee regarding the matter are still present, and the motion to
   reconsider is made by a member who voted with the prevailing side. A motion for

  reconsideration shall have precedence over every motion except a motion to

  adjourn. A final vote on any matter may also be placed on any future agenda for

  reconsideration by the Committee or any member of the Committee at the meeting

  at which the action was taken or at any later time. Any interested person may

  request that an action be reconsidered, provided that such a request must be in

  writing and filed with the Palmdale City Clerk within ten calendar days of the action

  of the Committee.

ARTICLE VI. - AMENDMENTS.

  Any amendment to these Bylaws shall be approved by a simple majority vote of the

  entire Committee and ratified by the City Council.

ISSUE
City Council Nomination and Appointment of Seven (7) Members and two (2) Alternates
to the Measure AV Oversight Committee.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council nominate and appoint individuals to serve as
Committee Members (7) and Alternates (2) on the Measure AV Oversight Committee for
a term to expire on April 30, 2025.

BACKGROUND
At the General Municipal Election held on November 3, 2020, voters approved the
enactment of a local ¾ cent transaction and use tax in the City of Palmdale. The measure
allowed for local control of sales tax dollars, long-term fiscal sustainability, and allowed
the City to continue to fund reliable essential services for the community. The revenues
and expenditures from the tax are to be regularly reviewed by a citizens advisory
committee to ensure the funds collected are expended for the purposes specified in the
Measure AV Ballot language and to provide enhanced transparency and public
participation. The City Council shall appoint a seven-member committee and by
resolution, adopt guidelines for the duties of a citizen’s oversight committee, later named
Measure AV Oversight Committee.

DISCUSSION
The terms for the current Measure AV Oversight Committee Members have expired. City
Council directed staff to open a recruitment for multiple positions on the Measure AV
Oversight Committee and notify current members that they would need to reapply if they
wished to continue to serve. Staff placed an advertisement in the AV Press, AV Press
Online, and posted the advertisement on the city’s website for interested citizens to apply.
The Communications Division also provided a press release to the public and posted the
advertisement on the city’s Social Media platforms. The recruitment ran January 31, 2023
through March 16, 2023, and was extended through April 23, 2023. Staff received

ISSUE
Presentation of City of Palmdale Proposed Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-24.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council, Chairs, Commissioners, Members and
Directors review the proposed budget and provide recommendation for adoption.
BACKGROUND
Each year the City is required to adopt a budget for the operation of the City. The budget
serves as the City’s financial plan for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1 through June 30.
It defines City priorities for the provision of services to the community.
According to the Palmdale Municipal Code: Chapter 3.04 Budget Adoption Procedures,
the City Manager shall submit a proposed budget to the City Council no later than May
31 each year. Additionally, the City Council shall conduct a public hearing on the
proposed budget before adoption and shall adopt a budget prescribing the spending
policy of the City for the ensuing fiscal year on or before the thirtieth day of June of each
year.
DISCUSSION
Staff is bringing forth the Proposed Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-24 for your review and
consideration.
The proposed Annual Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-24 represents spending plans for all
funds of the City, including General Fund, Special Revenue Funds, Capital Project Funds,
Internal Service Funds, and Enterprise Funds.

    Bilingual pay of $100 per month for eligible full-time and part-time staff

GENERAL FUND
Revenues
  1. Property Taxes are anticipated to increase by 5% due to property values
  increases.
  2. Sales Taxes are expected to increase by 1% based on economic performance
  in the City.
  3. Use of Property revenues are expected to increase by 13% as a result of rising
  interest rates, lease agreements and rental of City owned facilities.
  4. License and permits are expected to decrease by 13%, primarily in building
  permits as a result of a slow-down in development due to utility delays, rising
  interest rates, and inflationary pressure.
  5. Development charges for services are expected to decrease by 18% due to
  increases in plan checks and inspections during FY 2023 as a result of specific
  developments that are not anticipated in the coming year.
  6. Other revenues are expected to increase dramatically, by 116%, in FY 2024 as
  a result of a one-time economic development property sale.
Expenditures

  the result of FY 2023 projections being reduced to account for vacancy savings
  that have been realized throughout the year. FY 2024 proposed budget would
  fully fund those positions that have been filled or are currently in recruitment
  phases. The FY 2024 salary and benefits include a proposed 3% increase (2%
  COLA and 1% wage increase) to employees.
